points.text: Main-text figures use coded prompt labels defined only in appendix tables
No mechanistic explanation of why inoculation prompting works
Small-scale controlled datasets with narrow metrics; generalization beyond simple behaviors unshown
Improvements modest and possibly within fine-tuning variance
Effectiveness brittle across models, reversing with later training or larger models
Results highly sensitive to inoculation prompt wording, hurting reproducibility
Method is ad hoc prompt manipulation rather than algorithmic innovation
Near-total overlap with concurrent Tan et al. work weakens originality
Concurrent work covers more significant settings, making contribution incremental
Minor wording change in sycophancy prompt sharply reduces effectiveness; brittle
Requires a priori knowledge of undesired behavior; unforeseen behaviors untested
Tasks overly scriptable; real failures not nameable in one line untested
Prompt-selection heuristic assumes failure can be elicited; hard-to-elicit cases unanalysed
No OOD or compositional attack evaluation; evals isomorphic to training
Scope narrower than framing; reads as SFT data-engineering trick
Needs stronger baselines
Inoculation and evaluation prompts selected on reporting evaluation data; no validation split
Several secondary claims rest on single runs without training-seed variance
No significance test for IP vs baselines; 'significantly' untested
Elicitation-inoculation correlations pooled with unrelated prompts, no CIs, weak evidence
Hyperparameters, decoding, eval sizes and compute missing; preliminary experiments not shown
Claims of consistent outperformance and no capability loss exceed mixed results
Mixtral correlation 0.57 in text vs 0.60 in caption
'Above .57' wording while correlations equal .57
SFT-only on small LoRA models with constructed data, unlike RL motivation and title
Results figure-only; no summary table of effect sizes and prompt success counts
Reproducibility gaps: hyperparameters missing, code only promised
Empty appendix headings, garbled sentence, axis label issues
No causal analysis of when IP fails for co-occurring traits
Assumes developer knows and can name the undesired behavior
Assumes short SFT-scale training; effect weakens with longer mixed training
Side effect of increased compliance with harmful instructions unaddressed
Alignment evaluation narrow (single behaviors) relative to title
LLM and moderation-API judges lack human validation
No ethics or data-use statement for toxic Reddit training
Headline reward-hacking setting gains not explained by inoculation; prompts elicit no hacking
Theory assumes convergence contradicted by short training and weakening effects
Constant-k assumption tested only in small toy without fit statistic
Theoretical thresholds never compared with main experiments
No comparison to non-prompt methods like steering, ablation or filtering oracle
Context distillation and prompting-for-internalization prior work not discussed
Garbled final sentence of App. M
Prompts chosen by score on reporting evaluation; best-of-N unquantified, no dev split
Headline setting gains attributed to instruction-following, not inoculation
No conditioning-token control for explicit-rule alternative explanation
Title, abstract and 'consistently outperforms PTST' overclaim results
IP increases compliance with undesired requests in some models; single-run evidence
Motivated by RL reward hacking but evidence is SFT on constructed data
Mixtral correlation 0.57 vs 0.60 inconsistency
'Above .57' wording inaccurate
Unvalidated speculation about LLM judge behaviour
Constant-k assumption tested on toy with 32 points, no fit statistic

P.summary: Coded figure labels defined only in appendix
Gains modest and possibly within run variance
Effect brittle across models and training length
Overlap with concurrent work weakens originality
Incremental relative to concurrent work's settings
Requires behavior to be known and nameable

Q.summary: SFT-only small-model scope vs RL motivation
No analysis of when IP should not be used
